method: Automated inventory read every source, evidence, pathway, profile and review record in the exact manifest candidate for this ISO.

Automated screening compared source references, locators, geography fields, evidence class, direction, status, horizon and scenario; it checked pathway support IDs, link-evidence sets, geography fields, alternatives and uncertainty for follow-up.

Raw extraction access rows are recorded only as inherited access observations. This generated screen does not treat snippets, HTTP success, prior access, or metadata as claim verification and does not replace semantic source review.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2024-02-07 reports: During review, Belarus said its hydrometeorological network is updated annually but sanctions pressure had ended some bilateral agreements with neighbours for exchanging hydrometeorological information.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Section 2.1.1, paragraphs on historical seasonal runoff changes

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2020-12-18 reports: OECD reports earlier spring runoff nationwide since the 1980 s; cited records show maximum spring runoff fell 43% on average between 1877–1965 and 1966–2005, with Grodno more affected than Brest oblast.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.scenario: The OECD report gives a 2035 projection but does not specify the emissions pathway.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2020-12-18 reports: OECD reports that Pripyat runoff during Gomel's growing season could decline by up to 25% by 2035, partly due to climate-linked precipitation decline, intensifying seasonal water stress for agriculture.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2020-12-18 reports: In Kopyl rayon, OECD reports centralized water access for 98% of Kopyl town residents but 27% across rural settlements; many small communities rely on shallow wells with limited routine water-quality checks.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF p. 34, section 6.1.3, Polesie and Chornobyl

evidence.scenario: The hotspot assessment describes risk pathways; no emissions scenario is specified.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2017-11-09 reports: The regional assessment identifies southern Belarusian Polesie, including the Polesie State Radioecological Reserve, as a climate-security hotspot where drought and flood risks threaten livelihoods, health and local economic security.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF p. 34, section 6.1.3, paragraphs on Chornobyl contamination and monitoring

evidence.scenario: The assessment identifies conditional spread pathways without a quantified emissions scenario.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2017-11-09 reports: The assessment says irregular monitoring in the most contaminated areas undermines timely warnings and prevention as floods, drought, dust and fires could spread Chornobyl radionuclides across Polesie.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Article paragraphs on Homiel region's April 2020 drought and radioactive zone

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2020 reports: The UNCCD article reports 7.9 mm of rain in Homiel during the April 2020 planting season, 19% of normal, and says roughly 45% of the region lies in the Chornobyl-contaminated zone, making peat fires a public-health concern.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Article paragraphs on Greening Drylands Partnership implementation and second phase

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2020 reports: UNCCD reports about 1,000 ha of degraded peatland rewetted in Mogilev region in 2018–2019 with local-authority, forestry and community partnership; its 2020 Homiel phase targeted at least 2,000 ha and improved fire monitoring and early warning.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.
